subject: Novamed compliance onboarding — questions on audit/logs, KMS, SSO
messages:
From: Claire Tong <claire.tong@novamed.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@novamed.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Novamed compliance onboarding — initial questionnaire

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Novamed's compliance team reviewed the product overview and has a short set of follow-ups we need answered before we can progress the procurement paperwork. High level asks: audit/logging granularity, data retention policies (exportable evidence), BYOK/KMS workflow (rotation/escrow), and SSO provisioning (SCIM/SCIM groups).

I've attached our questionnaire (Novamed_compliance_q1.pdf) — it's only ~8 pages. Key near-term items:
- Can you confirm the minimum audit retention granularity (per-request, per-tenant, per-token)?
- Is there an off-ramp to export logs with timestamps and request/response ids?
- For BYOK, what key lifecycles do you support (rotation cadence + escrow)?
- How does SSO provisioning work for service accounts (SCIM + role mapping)?

Could you respond with a short answers doc and a recommended timeline? Novamed is aiming to close onboarding by next Friday.

Appreciate it — Claire

--
Claire Tong
Head of Security Operations | Novamed
[attachment: novamed_compliance_q1.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Novamed compliance onboarding — initial questionnaire

Hi Claire — thanks for the note and for the questionnaire. Looping in Marissa (product) and Jonas/Naomi (security/ops) so we can give concrete answers and ownership.

Quick plan:
1) We'll do a short written response to each question by EOD Thursday with references and example exports.
2) If there are gaps, propose a 30-min technical call Friday to walk the Novamed security team through the flows and tradeoffs.

Pre-reads we will attach: a brief evidence matrix (how to extract audit slices), and the BYOK lifecycle doc for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Immediate clarifying asks for you (so we target the right detail level):
- Are you asking for per-request bodies in the exported evidence, or are request/response ids + metadata sufficient?
- For BYOK, do you require escrow (we offer an optional escrow path) or is customer-managed rotation enough?

Assigning internal owners: Jonas — can you draft the retention/export options and list gaps? Naomi — can you pull the evidence matrix and any existing customer exports we can redact? Marissa — can you confirm product gating (what shipping paths we'd need to enable any new export/retention options)?

Sean
VP, Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Tong <claire.tong@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed compliance onboarding — initial questionnaire

Thanks Sean — quick product notes for the response doc. I'm keeping this high level so Ops can add implementation detail:

- Audit retention: product supports event-level logs (per-request metadata) and optional full request/response body capture behind a feature flag (requires legal review + customer opt-in).
- Export format: we can produce time-windowed exports (CSV/NDJSON) containing timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, model_id, input_hash, and metadata. Full bodies are available as separate export artifacts if enabled.
- BYOK/KMS: Dedicated and Private support CMKs in customer KMS. Rotation: we support 30/90/365-day rotation policies; escrow is an opt-in (we store a wrapped copy in secure escrow vault). Need legal signoff for escrow for some regions.
- SSO: SCIM v2 supported for user provisioning; service-account SCIM mapping will require a simple role mapping table (we'll provide an example).

Action items:
- Jonas: confirm whether the audit export preserves original request timestamps to millisecond precision and whether we can add a signed hash for tamper-evidence.
- Naomi: assemble redacted sample export (redwood_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx) and include sample CSV.
- Sean: propose the timeline to Claire once we have the samples.

I can own the go/no-go for shipping any export changes needed; if we need a small product effort (1–2 sprints) we'll flag that. If Ops can scope impact and rough ETA we can share a date with Novamed.

-Marissa
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Tong <claire.tong@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed compliance onboarding — initial questionnaire

Adding the Ops/tech perspective — notes and constraints below.

- Retention/export: current pipeline stores fine-grained audit events in the audit-stream with millisecond timestamps. We can slice by tenant_id + time window and export NDJSON with an HMAC per-file for tamper evidence. Full request bodies are stored in an encrypted blob store (default disabled for hosted tenants). Enabling bodies for export is possible but will require: 1) a short config toggle, 2) documentation updates, and 3) a gated rollout.
- BYOK/KMS: for Dedicated/Private we integrate with customer KMS via CMEK. We support key wrapping and rotation. Escrow flow exists as a manual emergency-key-rotation path and requires a signed escrow agreement (legal). For Hosted, we provide an encrypted-blob option with customer-supplied keys in a bring-your-own-keystore (BYOK) beta — note: the beta does not support escrow.
- SSO/service accounts: SCIM provisioning + group mapping works today for user accounts. Service accounts currently use token-based provisioning; adding SCIM for service accounts is feasible but will need an API extension (one sprint estimate, 2 engineers).

Proposed immediate deliverables (this week):
- Redacted sample exports (Naomi)
- Short answers doc with the HMAC example and BYOK caveats (me)
- Proposed timeline: initial written answers by Thu EOD (we'll hit this), follow-up 30-min call Fri if Novamed requests it, and product ticket creation next week if any feature work is required (I will create SUP-4721 for the export toggle + service-account SCIM).

-Jonas
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Claire — the review team flagged two clarifications:
1) We need request/response id + timestamp (ms) and a signed HMAC for tamper evidence on exported slices.
2) Escrow: Novamed intends to use escrow for long-term retention (>1 year) in the event of customer-side key loss — can you confirm Redwood's escrow process and where the legal agreement lives?

--
Claire

Could you confirm the two bullet points above in your write-up? If possible we'd prefer an ETA for when a gated export toggle (with body export and HMAC) could be available. Novamed needs a tentative timeline to include in their procurement packet.

Thanks again,
Claire
